title: Apple rescues Hide My Email feature from the privacy scrap heap
slides: Apple revives Hide My Email, but is privacy truly back?
The feature was nearly dead inside iCloud+ this year.
New design hides addresses even from Apple's own systems.
Your inbox now shields identity across every login automatically.
Activate it today, or watch your email leak tomorrow.
thread_text:
1. Apple's privacy was a lie?

Until this year, the company could still see the addresses you were hiding from spammers.

2. The almost-dead feature

iCloud+ nearly killed it in 2024. The new design is a complete reversal.

3. Now even Apple can't look

Your real address is replaced before it ever touches their servers.

4. Every login, auto-shielded

No more manual clicks. Every new account gets a fresh alias without you asking.

5. Activate it now, or leak

Go to iCloud+ settings today and enable it. If you skip it, your next signup is exposed.

instagram.caption:
Apple could still see the email addresses you were hiding from spammers — until now.

The old Hide My Email feature was nearly killed off this year. A full redesign flips that: your real address is stripped out before it ever touches Apple's own systems.

Even Apple's servers no longer see what you're protecting. Every new login gets a fresh alias automatically, no manual clicks needed.

If you create content, sponsor deals, or manage newsletter signups, this means your inbox stops being a leak point. The alias shields you before the first email ever lands.

Head to iCloud+ settings and switch it on today — or your next signup goes out naked. 🔐📧

When did you last check who actually sees your real address?
